task.description: TEST-DESIGNER (WF-02 Step 3) for REQ-160. ELIXIR-DEV already wrote 82 passing tests in test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs during Step 2a as basic self-verification, and both SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER passed the implementation. Your job is NOT to rubber-stamp that existing coverage -- it is to actively find real coverage gaps using MUTATION TESTING: deliberately break a small piece of lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex's new REQ-160 code (write_variable/call_service/emit_event and their helpers), run the existing test suite, and see whether it actually fails. If it doesn't fail, that's a real gap -- add a test that would have caught it, then revert your deliberate break. This project's track record this session: mutation testing has repeatedly found real gaps other passes missed (REQ-155's fixed-sleep race, REQ-156's untested timeout-during-memory-limited-call branch, REQ-158's hash self-comparison blind spot, REQ-159's return-value-correct-but-mechanism-unverified gap for zero-Repo-calls). Do the same here. Update test/specs/REQ-160.md (prose test spec) to match whatever final test file state you land on.
acceptance_criteria: Mutation-test write_variable's last-write-wins semantics: mutate Map.put to something that doesn't overwrite, confirm a test catches it.
Mutation-test take_staged_writes/0's clear-after-read behavior: mutate it to not clear, confirm a test catches a stale-buffer-on-second-call scenario.
Mutation-test call_service's never-raises property: mutate one error arm to raise instead of return, confirm a test catches it (not just a happy-path test that never exercises that arm).

Mutation-test the LUA-06-vs-LUA-12 distinction: mutate the capability check ordering (if trivially mutable) or confirm via a telemetry/mock spy that a missing-capability call truly never enters call_service's/emit_event's body at all -- not just that it happens to raise for some other reason.

Mutation-test emit_event's prefix discipline: mutate the append/2 call to use a script-supplied value instead of execution_context.prefix, confirm a test catches the wrong-tenant-schema outcome (this is the single highest-value test given SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS rested on this exact property).

Mutation-test the LuaNumberMarshalling.from_lua/1/to_lua/1 usage: mutate one call site to skip the conversion, confirm a test catches a value that would otherwise pass through unconverted (not just a test with an already-integer input where the mutation would be invisible).

Confirm zero-Repo-calls for write_variable/call_service is verified by a real mechanism (e.g. a Repo-call-count spy or telemetry, mirroring REQ-159's own precedent), not merely inferred from the return value being correct.

Every one of REQ-160's 8 real acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml) has at least one test that would fail if that specific behavior regressed -- verified by actually breaking it, not just present in the file.

result.summary: Ran 7 deliberate mutations against lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex, one per acceptance criterion (AC7's zero-Repo-calls got its own dedicated mutation on top of the 6 named ones). Each mutation was applied, mix test test/letflow/engine/lua/platform_test.exs was run and its result recorded, then the mutation was reverted (platform.ex is byte-identical to the pre-existing committed version: `git diff --stat lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex` is empty). Baseline before any TEST-DESIGNER addition: 82 tests passing. Final state: 85 tests passing, all against the real (unmutated) implementation. Full detail, including the exact mutated line and exact pass/fail counts for every mutation, is in test/specs/REQ-160.md's 'Mutation-testing findings' section.

78/82 passed, 4 failures (multiple existing tests exercise this arm, including the default NoServiceCaller path)

mutations.action: GAP CLOSED: added SpyServiceCaller (a ServiceCaller double that send/2's a message when invoked) plus a call_service test asserting refute_received after a denied call; and an emit_event test using a Repo-query telemetry counter asserting zero queries fire for a denied call made with a FULLY POPULATED execution context (prefix/instance_id/actor_id all set, a real registered event type) so the body, if reached, would genuinely attempt a Repo call via EventStore.append/2. Both new tests fail against the reordered mutation (82/84, both new tests in the failure list) and pass against the real code (85/85).

mutations.action: none needed -- this is the property SECURITY-REVIEWER's PASS rests on and it is already well covered by both a functional and a structural test

mutations.result: 84/84 passed unchanged, including the existing float-specific round-trip test -- LuaNumberMarshalling.from_lua/1 and .to_lua/1 are BOTH literal identity functions (def from_lua(value), do: value, per REQ-150's own normative identity rule), so no behavioral test of any input shape can ever distinguish 'called the identity function' from 'skipped it'
mutations.action: GAP CLOSED, by a structural test rather than a behavioral one (behavioral detection is impossible by construction given REQ-150's identity rule): added a source-inspection test asserting every REQ-160 numeric-crossing call site (do_write_variable/2, normalize_from_lua/1, convert_map_to_lua/1) textually invokes LuaNumberMarshalling.from_lua/.to_lua by name, plus a floor count (>=3 each) on total occurrences. This test fails (84/85) when the call is removed and passes (85/85) against the real code.

mutations.action: none needed -- confirms the existing zero-Repo-calls telemetry-counter mechanism (mirroring REQ-159's own precedent) is a genuine spy that fires on a real injected Repo call, not merely inferred from a correct return value
